Project/sequence progress displays completed real flash operations; short RAM-only sequence loads may complete immediately.

DMA deadline, flash timing and UI timing require physical FM1 validation.
V1.29 settings navigation plus V1.28 storage, USB disconnect and screensaver need physical FM1 verification by the author.
WIPE ALL irreversibly erases known user storage 0x97000..0xDFFFF, including legacy stored data; it does NOT erase application/boot/OTA sectors or unknown flash areas.

Deleting the active project and the final remaining project is supported. A shared wave-library owner cannot be deleted while other projects depend on it; delete dependent projects first or back up and use WIPE ALL.
Managing sequences in a different project requires explicitly opening that project first (confirmation on FM1).
Scan the source white-on-black QR on a physical FM1 after updating; software verifies exact source parity, not every phone camera inversion capability.
Utrecht screensaver, configurable timeout, REC LED hardware mapping and physical refresh must be verified on an actual FM1.

Per-sequence BPM and length are reliably retained only for sequences saved with V1.33 or later. Older sequences lack a trustworthy per-sequence metadata marker; loading uses the last project values. If a previous failed save never committed note data to flash, the new firmware cannot recover that unsaved data.
V1.36 WIPE ALL and final-project DELETE are host NOR-tested only; verify on real hardware before relying on them.
Shared-waveform-owner projects cannot be deleted while other projects depend on them. Delete dependent projects first, or back up and perform confirmed WIPE ALL.
AUTO LOAD defaults to NEW and is journaled with master volume/autosave/screensaver; actual cold boot must be physically verified.
V1.38 prepared coefficient reuse preserves all four filter kernels sample-exactly; actual FM1 DMA margin and reported crackling/audio stops are not independently verified on physical hardware.
RUPTURE monophonic DMA adaptation prioritizes UI/scope suppression before continued deadlines; persistent DMA misses still trigger the original safety stop.

V1.39 fixes a confirmed DSP hot-path defect: enabled but flat Channel EQ 2.0 previously disabled full FX dry bypass and processed four Q26 biquads; new dry unity and per-band neutral paths are proven in host tests, but FM1 DMA timing/physical crackle are not yet verified.
V1.39 targets the no-filter/no-effects audio regression; intermittent hardware DMA stops require reading AUDIO DIAGNOSTICS on the actual FM1 to prove resolution.

V1.40 fixes off-state wet algorithm CPU waste across chorus/delay/reverb when other effects are enabled; all twelve host FX PCM parity cases match V1.39, but physical FM1 DMA stops and full multi-FX soak remain to be verified.
New unsaved projects default EQ2 to bypass OFF. Previously saved projects keep original EQ-on/off and sound. Firmware update does not wipe project storage.

V1.41 corrects excessive EQ2 auto-trim (-36 dB possible at four boosts), EQ OFF dry parity, and active EQ coefficient-update cost. FM1 physical DMA and audio quality must still be verified. Peak guard only acts near clipping.

V1.42 smooths OCTAVE FUZZ gain, drive, octave and tone changes at sample rate, softens the rectifier zero crossing, and replaces its periodic variable division with a fixed reciprocal lookup. The original clipping character is retained. Real FM1 listening and DMA timing must still be verified.

V1.43 OTA native tests demonstrate a residual LOADER.BIN recovery route, but exact official stock V15 full-session replay and device-specific physical FM1 transitions have not been validated. On a bootheader mismatch the official V15 downgrade is refused to avoid unsafe boot writes; use a validated USB ROM rescue rather than forcing an unsafe flash.

V1.44 supports the exact archived official M-VAVE V15 eight-entry firmware (SHA-256 db1642b2b6fa5c2cccb11ffd13878068bb28601678d3644049f99dc40e7edb8a). Native OTA host replay reaches handoff; full on-device stock install has not been physically verified and requires backup/rescue readiness.
SAW/SQUARE generator and screensaver are host-tested; no independent real-FM1 DMA profiling has been performed for V1.45.

V1.46 PLAY and SOUND SHAPE native header spacing verified in host pixel export; SAW controls and shared saved knob values tested on host, not on physical FM1 DMA. Four SAW dial roles are BRIGHT, EDGE, BODY and LEVEL. They reuse the four legacy macro values; CXS macro settings therefore reflect changes made in SAW mode.

V1.47 makes all four SOUND SHAPING knobs audibly modify sustained SAW; dedicated SAW shaping bypasses the 64-bit CXS shaper when SAW is fully selected. All four were verified over long sustained host PCM tests with UBSan; physical FM1 output and worst-case DMA margin have not been measured.

V1.48 restores SAVE project-browser access from all ordinary UI screens except sequencer and protected name/OTA/recovery actions; source routing audit covers all 49 page IDs. Physical button events remain unverified.

V1.48 strong-SA W harmonic guard reduces spectral aliases in host tests at fully raised parameters, but intentionally softens upper harmonics during strong nonlinear shaping. No physical FM1 noise/speaker/DMA tests have been performed.

V1.49 DAM animation uses exact user PNG pixels (10080 static sprite bytes), LCD blits are UI-only and FM1 physical frame timing, SPI/USB/audio under stress must be validated. No audio or flash storage schema changes.

V1.53 CRT defaults OFF if no saved CRT value exists; explicitly saved ON from older firmware remains ON until toggled OFF. The unfiltered 1-bit display path is used at default.

V1.54 DAM V3 uses 20 exact bitmaps (16800 flash bytes), a new UI-only animation timetable and no changes to audio core, audio ISR, synthesizer DSP, project serialization, bootheader or updater. Physical LCD/audio timing needs validation.

The first-run storage format is always optional; destructive initialization only follows YES and three seconds of SAVE hold. For already-valid RUPTURE project storage the wizard does not format again.
If the user skips formatting with unavailable/foreign storage, the completion flag cannot be written safely. The wizard may therefore return at the next boot.
CRT preference and first-run completion reside in the existing CRC-protected global settings NOR journal. Physical cold-boot and storage-format testing remains necessary.
V1.60 first-run format confirmation has host tests; physical FM1 storage formatting and display remain unverified.

V1.63 one-gesture UNDO is intentionally limited to simple single-byte knob controls (PLAY, SHAPE, SUB, TILT, FUZZ, SANDPAPER); it does not support sequence, composite filter, or project-wide undo. Physical controls and project-load safety require FM1 hardware validation.
V1.79: 32-bit DSP optimizations and LCD batching pass host PCM and native-build checks; device-specific DSP %, DMA LATE, GUARD and crackle-free live performance are not yet hardware verified.

V1.80: ROOM and SPRING use distinct more sophisticated global delay networks; credibility on speakers and hardware DMA deadlines is not certified. ROOM may increase CPU vs V1.79 despite fixed-point optimizations. Do not use as live/studio guaranteed stable without testing on FM1.
V1.81 host PCM tests prove parity but not FM1 real-time worst-case cycle budget; rapid LCD transfers are reduced; physical DMA LATE/GUARD stability remains unverified.
V1.82 and stock V15 round-trip to the exact same V1.82 cannot always be detected if stock preserves the setup marker; FM1 hardware verification required.
V1.83: host PCM parity does not prove zero LATE/GUARD on FM1. Full maximum-param stress and hardware measurements are still required.
V1.84: native build and host LED/button checks do not prove physical FM1 LED brightness, audio headroom or zero LATE/GUARD; hardware verification remains required.

V1.84.1: LED startup current-step reduction is verified in source and host tests, but a speaker pop can also originate in PC6 analog-output enable; physical audio measurements are required before claiming the pop eliminated.
V1.84.2: source/host tests prove LED current-edge and PC6 sequencing, not removal of an intrinsic amplifier-bias pop; low-volume physical FM1 testing remains essential.

V1.85: only exceptional >32-event MIDI burst input can be deferred by 1+ 128-sample audio halves; queue overflow panic protection remains. Host test does not prove zero DMA LATE/GUARD, no speaker pop or worst-case USB+TRS MIDI stability on real FM1 hardware.

V1.85: only exceptional >32-event MIDI burst input can be deferred by 1+ 128-sample audio halves; queue overflow panic protection remains. Host test does not prove zero DMA LATE/GUARD, no speaker pop or worst-case USB+TRS MIDI stability on real FM1 hardware.
